title: System Explorer capability discovery
description: What this host can answer for, and a stated reason for anything it cannot (SPEC section 2, rule 7: absence is not an error). Every consumer starts here — the UI generates its nav from this document, so a subsystem's availability decides whether it is offered at all, and the MCP list_hosts tool returns the same per configured agent. Absence is reported at two levels: a whole subsystem declines with a reason, and an available subsystem may still decline individual collections through unavailable_collections. Shared $defs are duplicated from observation.schema.json deliberately so each schema file is standalone.

version.description: Agent version. Absent from an agent predating the field; a hub reports it per host so a mid-rollout estate is visible as such rather than as inexplicably differing behaviour.

revision.description: Source revision the agent was built from. Absent when the build did not record one.

site.description: Where this host's site view lives, if the deployment configured one. A DISPLAY HINT the deployment supplies, never discovery: the agent does not find its hub and never talks to it, because aggregation must never be a precondition for observation (SPEC section 7, ROADMAP section 6). Absent means no hub was configured, not that none exists.

subsystems.description: Subsystem name -> capability. Every subsystem the agent knows appears, including those it cannot serve; a subsystem declared in SPEC section 4 with no adapter yet appears here as unavailable with a reason rather than being silently missing.

subsystemCapability.description: Two invariants rather than an enumeration of shapes: an available subsystem names its collections, and an unavailable one says why.

collections.description: Collections this subsystem can serve right now. Excludes anything in unavailable_collections.

unavailable_collections.description: Collection name -> why this host cannot serve it, while the subsystem as a whole works. Keys are NOT constrained to the collections array, and are not a subset of it: a collection may be advertised here that the subsystem does not otherwise list.

manager.description: The package manager this host resolves to (nix, dpkg, rpm). Emitted by the packages subsystem only; declared here because the producer profile closes what it validates, so an undeclared member fails CI.

reason.description: Why this subsystem cannot be served: a missing socket, an absent daemon, a failed capability probe, or no adapter yet.

allOf.description: Available means it says what it can serve.
Unavailable means it says why. An absence with no reason is the v0.1 mistake this rule exists to prevent.
